symbols.name: source transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized transform $F_q$ with $q=s$, acting on vectors of $s$ coordinates.
symbols.quote: Write $F_s$ and $F_t$ for $F_q$ with $q=s$ and $q=t$, the normalized transforms of vectors of $s$ and $t$ coordinates, and $F_s^+$ for the opposite transform $F_q^+$ with $q=s$.

symbols.name: target transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized transform $F_q$ with $q=t$, acting on vectors of $t$ coordinates.
symbols.quote: Write $F_s$ and $F_t$ for $F_q$ with $q=s$ and $q=t$, the normalized transforms of vectors of $s$ and $t$ coordinates, and $F_s^+$ for the opposite transform $F_q^+$ with $q=s$.

symbols.name: opposite source transform
symbols.meaning: The opposite transform $F_q^+$ with $q=s$, which uses $\omega^{-1}$ in place of $\omega$.
symbols.quote: Write $F_s$ and $F_t$ for $F_q$ with $q=s$ and $q=t$, the normalized transforms of vectors of $s$ and $t$ coordinates, and $F_s^+$ for the opposite transform $F_q^+$ with $q=s$.

symbols.name: coordinate count
symbols.meaning: The number of coordinates of the grid, a count.
symbols.quote: Here $d$ is the number of coordinates, not the digit count.

symbols.name: source axis length
symbols.meaning: The number of entries along coordinate $i$ of the source grid, a count.
symbols.quote: Here $s_i$ and $t_i$ are the numbers of entries along coordinate $i$ of the source and target grids.

symbols.name: target axis length
symbols.meaning: The number of entries along coordinate $i$ of the target grid, a count.
symbols.quote: Here $s_i$ and $t_i$ are the numbers of entries along coordinate $i$ of the source and target grids.

symbols.name: source permutation
symbols.meaning: The tensor product of the one-dimensional source permutations $P_{s_i}$, permuting the source coordinates.
symbols.quote: Here $R=\bigotimes_i P_{s_i}$ permutes the source coordinates, and $Q=\bigotimes_i P_{t_i}$ permutes the target coordinates.

symbols.name: target permutation
symbols.meaning: The tensor product of the one-dimensional target permutations $P_{t_i}$, permuting the target coordinates.
symbols.quote: Here $R=\bigotimes_i P_{s_i}$ permutes the source coordinates, and $Q=\bigotimes_i P_{t_i}$ permutes the target coordinates.

symbols.name: index permutation
symbols.meaning: The permutation $(R_c z)_j=z_{cj}$ of length-$q$ vectors, for a unit $c$ modulo $q$.
symbols.quote: Write $R_c$ for the permutation $(R_c z)_j=z_{cj}$ of length-$q$ vectors, where $c$ is a unit modulo $q$.

symbols.name: source-to-target contraction
symbols.meaning: The tensor product of the one-dimensional contractions $A$, mapping source arrays to target arrays.
symbols.quote: The letters $A$ and $B_0$ denote the one-dimensional contractions below, and after lifting they denote tensor products.

symbols.name: target-to-source contraction
symbols.meaning: The tensor product of the one-dimensional contractions $B_0$, mapping target arrays to source arrays.
symbols.quote: The letters $A$ and $B_0$ denote the one-dimensional contractions below, and after lifting they denote tensor products.

symbols.name: source array
symbols.meaning: An array on the source grid of shape $s_1\times\cdots\times s_d$.
symbols.quote: The arrays $u$ and $v$ now live on the source grid of shape $s_1\times\cdots\times s_d$.

symbols.name: second source array
symbols.meaning: A second array on the source grid of shape $s_1\times\cdots\times s_d$.
symbols.quote: The arrays $u$ and $v$ now live on the source grid of shape $s_1\times\cdots\times s_d$.

symbols.name: cyclic convolution
symbols.meaning: The cyclic convolution of two arrays on the source grid.
symbols.quote: Writing $u*v$ for the cyclic convolution on the source grid.

symbols.name: coordinatewise product
symbols.meaning: The product of two arrays taken entry by entry on the same grid.
symbols.quote: Permutations commute with coordinatewise products, so $(RF_su)\cdot(RF_sv)=R\big((F_su)\cdot(F_sv)\big)$, where $\cdot$ is the coordinatewise product.

relations.quote: The one-dimensional identity is derived from [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md).
The one-dimensional identity holds for [coprime](coprime-integers.md) $s<t$ with $\theta=t/s-1$ large enough: $P_sF_s=2^{2\alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA$, with contractions $A$ and $B_0$.
The identity is lifted by a [tensor product](tensor-product.md) of the one-dimensional identities to $d$ coordinates.
The cancellation is based on the [convolution theorem](convolution-theorem.md): with the $1/q$ factor of $F_q$, $F_s(u*v)=\left(\prod_i s_i\right)(F_su)\cdot(F_sv)$.
